items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I really didn't know the man until I had known him for quite a while. He used to love to play pool... So every day he used to play me for $2.

ctx.x: I'm not trying to stand by saying he's a Jewish. I never read of an opinion so biased in my life, you know, because of. Now, you see, but it's one thing, though. You know what you're going to find. You're always going to find that it's mediocre talent that talks that way. I'm a Christian. You see, if they'd have asked Duke Ellington about jelly, if he wouldn't have gave him no great ovation, he still wouldn't have brought him down the drain. Duke would have said, well, yeah, it sounds like great music for its…
No. I want to hear a bad man about it. I want to see if you want to talk about Aaron Harris. Yeah, well, it's not one of you. Yeah, this is Aaron. That was a bad boy. Did you?

I knew him. Yeah. You knew him too, huh? Oh, yeah, I knew him. What do you think they're talking about? It was a punk like him. It was Toodlam. It was Aaron Harris. It was Frenchy. Oh, it was Johnny Ray. It was Tom Leon. I mean, these were bad boys. You see, when the cop wanted Aaron, they wouldn't take him up like they'd pick up nobody. They'd tell him the chief want to see him. Yeah. I'll be there tomorrow, tell him. They tricked him out of his life. You see, uh... Yeah, they tricked him out of his life. If…
